name: Necros
label: Touch and Go
lede: Skate-park kids from a Toledo suburb put out Touch and Go's first record, lent their drummer to the Misfits for the last show of the original lineup, and handed the label to the bassist who ran it for decades.

eras.title: Skateboards first, band second
eras.text: Necros came out of Maumee, Ohio, a suburb of Toledo, though the punk world filed them under Detroit. The members skated before they played, and the band started as talk on the drive home from the park.

years.h: Necros starts on a ride home from the skate park in Maumee
years.p: Barry Henssler, Todd Swalla and Andy Wendler are Maumee skaters. Swalla says the band was born in the car, then practiced in his basement for a couple of years.
years.xp:
Swalla's mother taught music in the Toledo public schools and put up with the noise. Swalla told No Echo he first got on a board in 1969, "a pink piece of wood the shape of a hot dog with roller skate wheels nailed to it."

Necros went through four bassists before Corey Rusk: David Cooke, Brian Hyland, Jeff Lake and Brian Pollack, who later switched to guitar.

eras.title: The first band on Touch and Go
eras.text: A zine in the mail put Necros in front of Tesco Vee and Dave Stimson, who were turning their East Lansing fanzine, Touch and Go, into a label. Necros made its first release and brought in Corey Rusk, who ended up owning the whole thing.

years.h: Henssler mails Smegma Journal to Tesco Vee
years.p: Barry Henssler sends his zine to Vee and Dave Stimson of the Touch and Go fanzine. They like Necros and decide to put out a record.

years.h: Sex Drive becomes Touch and Go's first record
years.p: Four songs. About 25 sleeves in a Sex Pistols-style design got printed before the idea was dropped.
years.xp:
The Punk Vault says the leftover originals were thrown out when Stimson's parents redecorated. Reproductions from the original plates were made later.

Sources disagree on the pressing size, so none is given here.

years.h: Corey Rusk joins on bass, and the label comes with him
years.p: [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]] becomes Necros' bassist in 1981 and joins Tesco Vee in running Touch and Go the same year.

years.h: Ian MacKaye produces IQ32 for Touch and Go and Dischord
years.p: Nine songs, produced by [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]'s [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and released jointly by the two labels. Three pressings of 1,000 came out on green, tan and white labels.
years.xp: Dischord numbered it 4 1/2. A special run of 100 came in hand-numbered sleeves for a show at the Endless Summer skatepark.

years.h: Conquest for Death is the first Necros LP
years.p: A Touch and Go album, with a 7-inch of the same name. [[Pushead|404f318c-a6c4-43ed-892a-a431d0ad4b2b]] drew the artwork for the single.

years.src: Wikipedia: Touch and Go Records · The Punk Vault
years.h: Rusk quits the band to run the label full time
years.p: Tesco Vee leaves Michigan in 1983 and hands Touch and Go to Corey Rusk and his wife Lisa. Ron Sakowski takes over on bass.
years.xp:
The Punk Vault says Rusk and Barry Henssler would end up hating each other. It also says the band's infighting has kept the catalog out of print.

The Rusks later moved Touch and Go to Chicago.

years.h: Todd Swalla sits in for the Misfits at their last show
years.p: Necros open for the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]] at Graystone Hall in Detroit. The Misfits' drummer can't play, so Swalla takes the kit for the last show of the original lineup.
years.xp:
Swalla told No Echo it was his second time covering for the Misfits: he had rehearsed twice with them for an Irving Plaza show in New York. Detroit was spontaneous. "Necros played great and kids were insane!" he said.

The clip is a full Necros set from the Graystone in 1983; the uploader doesn't say it is the Misfits night.

eras.title: Slower, heavier, gone
eras.text: With Rusk at the label, Necros got heavier and slower, and Henssler kept it going with bigger plans. They opened for Black Flag, Bad Brains, Minor Threat and Sonic Youth, then toured with metal bands chasing a major-label deal that never came.

years.h: Necros splits Jail Jello with White Flag
years.p: The 12-inch is shared with [[White Flag|ad82f8fd-206f-4b62-9a0d-f46557edb725]]. The Tangled Up 7-inch follows, and both come out on Gasatanka.

years.h: A manager puts Necros on the bill with Megadeth and Overkill
years.p: Necros tours with [[Megadeth|a9044915-8be3-4c7e-b11f-9e2d2ea0a91e]] and [[Overkill|97fa7dd1-4706-4fad-b6ff-e099a37837fc]] and plays the Olympic Auditorium with [[Motörhead|57961a97-3796-4bf7-9f02-a985a8979ae9]] and [[Die Kreuzen|7550b236-f9c2-450c-81a6-fac63bf9d23e]]. Swalla says Megadeth drummer Chuck Behler later wore a Necros shirt on an album.
years.xp: Swalla's account: "Our manager booked Megadeth on that tour so they inserted us in the bill."

years.h: Tangled Up is the last Necros album
years.p: A metal-leaning second LP, on Restless.

years.big: It just felt like it was time to pack it in.
years.h: Elektra says no, and Necros calls it quits
years.p: Todd Swalla on the 1987 breakup, after most of 1986 on tour and a rejection from Elektra.

eras.title: Other bands, same scene
eras.text: The members turned up in the Detroit scene's next bands, and the label their old bassist ran grew into one of the biggest independents in America before scaling back in 2009.

years.h: Live or Else arrives three years late
years.p: A Necros live album on Medusa, out after the breakup. Rykodisc later paired it with Tangled Up on the band's only CD, in 2005.

years.h: Henssler forms Big Chief, Swalla and Sakowski join Laughing Hyenas
years.p: [[Big Chief|9e590e39-4fd6-4189-bfec-b698056a6999]] records for Sub Pop. [[Laughing Hyenas|a3e6d60a-34ff-4d99-8397-2db6b5b2333e]], on Touch and Go, are fronted by [[John Brannon|a3418f6c-a8b1-4565-9836-b389b405510a]] of [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]].

years.h: Sakowski plays bass for the reunited Negative Approach
years.p: Ron Sakowski joins [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]] when the Detroit band gets back together.

years.h: Rusk shuts down Touch and Go's manufacturing and distribution
years.p: Former Necros bassist Corey Rusk blames the economy and scales the label back.

years.h: Three Necros and a new singer play two shows as SorceN
years.p: Swalla, Wendler and Sakowski are joined by Eric Oblander on vocals.
